answer: Money leaves a paper trail, so tie each identity to one verified bank account. To enroll, the agent reports an account; the network sends two micro-deposits, and the agent must return their exact amounts within a day. An open-banking check confirms the account is unique and in good standing. A duplicate freezes both identities and holds their earnings pending review, while a fraud report closes the account. Opening 10,000 KYC-checked accounts costs about $50 each, $500,000 in all. Like a river cutting one canyon, one account carves one path; ivory-tower anonymity washes away.
